During floods, rivers spread beyond their channels, depositing layers of fertile silt that enrich surrounding soil. Tributaries add water and carve smaller valleys into the landscape, creating branching drainage systems. Over thousands or millions of years, these processes can transform mountains and plateaus into broad lowlands.
